records.region: South-central Newfoundland: Meelpaeg Reservoir, Grey River and the Grey River coastal inlet.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected southwestern outlet follows Grey River below the Pudops outlet setting, not the separate eastward diversion to the Salmon River/Bay d’Espoir power route. White Bear River lies farther west. The downstream selection contains the Grey River marine inlet as well as the freshwater river.
records.completion_scope: All 45 ordered parts of the sole mainstem fragment, their joins, the chosen headward lake chain, reservoir passage, western managed outlet setting, upper/middle/lower Grey River and the actual marine-inlet terminal were considered and geographically accounted for at ordinary corridor scale.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative Grey River drainage/corridor identity, including the selected unnamed upper lake chain, Meelpaeg reservoir passage, Pudops outlet, lower Grey River and the Grey River marine inlet. It is not one natural-river name for every component.

scope_limits: The name is a representative system identity, not a verified formal registry entry or scalar name for all stored parts.
Small selected headward lakes and connectors remain unnamed in the consulted cartography; their ordinary geographic correspondence is established.
The model includes reservoir and marine-inlet sections; its 141.988 km is not a surveyed length of natural Grey River.
The selected western exit is geographically accounted for despite the altered drainage. Present releases, lake levels and dam operation are outside this naming task.
Generalized management maps and historical engineering cartography are adequate at corridor scale; no exact-bank, exact-estuary-boundary or current-flow assertion is made.

records.region: Paraíba, Brazil: Esperança–Remígio northern approach through Araçagi to the lower Mamanguape estuary.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative receiving-system identity with separately named northern upstream components.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The chosen northern Covão/Araçagi approach is distinct from the southern Mamanguape headwaters. Rio Paraíba is a separate basin south of this route. The modeled terminal is not relocated to the Atlantic opening.
records.completion_scope: Ordinary river-corridor correspondence is complete for the supplied fragment and all 37 stored parts. Coarse bends and estuary-side endpoint generalization are retained without exact-bank, present-flow or operation requirements. Distinct labels are component observations, not aliases forced onto every segment.
records.supported_name_scope: Covão–Araçagi approach, Araçagi impoundment and receiving Mamanguape lower river/estuarine corridor; not a uniform name for every stored reach.

naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Lower Mamanguape estuary-side setting near Barra do Mamanguape, before the outer Atlantic opening.
naming_scope_details.access_limitations: Optional ICMBio management-plan catalogue unavailable. Independent AESA/SUDEMA and municipal originals supply the geographic correspondence; no second pending classification is created.

records.region: Trujillo and the southeastern Lago de Maracaibo shore; Carache/Monay approach, Agua Viva and lower Motatán
records.material_pending_reason: The chosen eastern opening, northwest-to-southwest return and northward upper connector into the westward lowland inflow are not continuously depicted in the inspected originals. Basin membership and Carache headwater prose cannot close those channel links.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The actual receiver is Lago de Maracaibo. The southern Motatán mountain approach and northern Jirajara approach are distinct from the selected eastern inflow. Paují, also discussed as Motatán de los Negros in regional prose, is a separate northern drainage and is not adopted as this feature’s alias.
records.completion_scope: Bounded name research finished with supported lower/reservoir/terminal correspondence and explicit upper-route material gaps. No new access failure; no accepted name or product change.
records.supported_name_scope: Supported for the westward receiving corridor below Agua Viva to Lago de Maracaibo. The eastern approach has separate Carache/Monay source usages; its full selected opening remains unestablished.

scope_limits: One material-pending status covers the unresolved eastern opening and upper connector; this is not a completed naming-scope hold.
Río Carache, Río Monay and Monaicito are retained in their actual source contexts without unsupported alias equivalence.
No full-feature scalar name, official registry decision, exact name-transition point, modern reservoir operation or current-flow claim is made.
Generalized regional maps establish the reservoir and receiver, but do not supply the omitted upper channel links.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
